STT-0421.title: Trolley canal boats
STT-0421.desc_html: In the early 20th century, several European countries electrified canal barge haulage by running trolley wires along towpaths, replacing horse teams with electric motors on the boats. The system was efficient and eliminated animal cruelty, but was killed by road trucking and the general decline of inland waterway freight after WWII

STT-0423.title: Chain-hauled steam river tugs
STT-0423.label: Chain boats / Kettenschleppschiffe / toueurs; La Ville de Sens (M. Dietz, c.1850); Elbe, Neckar, Main, Seine, Danube, c.1850–1950
STT-0423.desc_html: Steam river tugs hauling themselves and barge strings along a steel chain laid on the riverbed, suited to shallow, fast-flowing rivers. Prototyped in M. Dietz's La Ville de Sens (c.1850), they spread across Europe until more powerful paddle steamers and canalisation displaced them.

STT-0424.label: Churchill Crocodile / M67 Zippo
STT-0424.desc_html: Flame tanks: tanks fitted with flamethrowers (e.g. Churchill Crocodile, M67 Zippo), used widely in WWII against fortifications; range under 150 m, and late-war infantry anti-tank weapons outranged them. Out of the US arsenal since 1978, replaced by thermobaric and other incendiary weapons.

STT-0432.title: Land mines
STT-0432.desc_html: Even though many great powers did not sign the Ottawa mine ban treaty in 1997, its entry still had a marked effect. In the '90s, 25,000 people were killed or injured by land mines each year; by 2013, that number had fallen to 3,300., and tens of millions of mines have been destroyed. (more recently, this has slightly reversed, with annual landmine deaths and injuries rising to 5,700 in 2023)
STT-0432.sources_html: The Guardian, reliefweb.int, hrw.org

STT-0433.title: Automated electronic-sensor battlefield
STT-0433.label: Operation Igloo White, 1968–73
STT-0433.desc_html: Attempted battlefield awareness through >20,000 air-dropped sensors scattered across the Ho Chi Minh Trail, to direct strike aircraft. The North Vietnamese fooled with animals, urine buckets, and recordings; (source). As Kevin Baker notes: ''The system could be fooled because nobody in the process could look at what it was sensing. The Air Force claimed forty-six thousand trucks destroyed or damaged over the course of the campaign. The CIA reported that the claims for a single year exceeded the total number of trucks believed to exist in all of North Vietnam.22 The system’s own output was the only measure of its performance, and nobody outside the system had standing to challenge it. Air Force historian Bernard Nalty later called the service’s casualty computations “an exercise in metaphysics rather than mathematics” and his colleague Earl Tilford concluded that ’the Air Force succeeded only in fooling itself” the programme was working.""
STT-0433.sources_html: Air & Space Forces, Wikipedia, artificialbureaucracy (Substack)

STT-0445.label: low-tech sewage treatment
STT-0445.desc_html: For centuries and up to the mid 20th century, cities in Asia and parts of Europe treated sewage by channelling it through fish ponds — the fish consumed organic waste, produced edible protein, and the effluent emerged cleaner. The practice was eliminated by modern centralised sewage treatment, though it was often more resource-efficient. (source)

STT-0446.desc_html: Used in various cities (London Post Office Railway; Chicago tunnel system) for transportation without surface congestion (source)

STT-0451.label: Roman fermented fish sauce
STT-0451.desc_html: An industrial-scale condiment of the Roman world, produced in factories across the Mediterranean, that vanished with the collapse of Roman trade networks. Analogous to modern fish sauce (and arguably its ancestor), it illustrates how a food technology can disappear when the logistics infrastructure supporting it collapses. (source)

STT-0495.title: DDT insecticide for agriculture and vector control
STT-0495.desc_html: Synthetic insecticide discovered in 1939 by Paul Müller's team at Geigy; it underpinned national malaria-spraying campaigns. Insect resistance emerged from 1947, and documented harms to birds, fish and wildlife, publicised by Rachel Carson's Silent Spring (1962), led to agricultural phase-outs and bans in many countries.
STT-0495.sources_html: Works in Progress

STT-0453.title: 'Peaceful Nuclear Explosions' for civil engineering applications
STT-0453.desc_html: Between 1965-1988, the USSR conducted 122 nuclear explosions (yields from 0.01 to 140kt, vast majority 2-20kt) to study 13 applications; over half used for the creation of underground cavities in salt for the storage of gas condensate and deep seismic sounding. Also included limited but failed attempts to change the course of rivers. Chernobyl killed the project politically, and the tests were ended as part of a unilateral Soviet moratorium on nuclear weapons testing adopted by Gorbachev.
STT-0453.sources_html: scienceandglobalsecurity.org, BBC

STT-0474.title: OSI X.400 message handling with built-in encryption
STT-0474.desc_html: Message Handling System of the telecom-industry OSI protocol suite (published 1984; 1988 Blue Book), using ASN.1 encoding and X.500/X.509 directory-based public keys for end-to-end encryption. More efficient than many alternatives but lost to SMTP internet email, because ASN.1 messaging failed and no global directory materialised; survives in military, ICAO aviation, EDI.

STT-0058.title: Numerous proposals for anti-satellite (ASAT) weapons
STT-0058.desc_html: Including proposals focusing on: air-launched interceptors (1961–63)
STT-0058.subs_html:
• Soyuz-P (manned inspect-and-destroy) — rejected; EVA against a satellite presumed to have an automatic self-destruct was effectively suicide.
  • Soyuz 7K-PPK (manned stand-off with rocket-mines) — dropped after Soyuz development delays and success of the unmanned kamikaze tests.
  • Unmanned interceptor with mine-rockets — abandoned; same guidance-accuracy problem, plus the interceptor exposed itself to counter-ASATs during approach.
  • Lurking on-orbit interceptors — paper only; needed an oversized engine/fuel load, ≤12-month storage life, and would themselves be ASAT targets.
  • Multi-target mine dispenser (12 interceptors per launch) — rejected as prohibitively large and expensive despite optimal targeting economics.

STT-0472.desc_html: During World War II, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office deployed its Compulsory Invention Secrecy doctrine to withold patent rights for more than 11,000 patent applications, prohibiting their disclosure to prevent technology leakage. While these orders were rescinded en masse at the end of the war, it caused firms to shift their patenting away from the affected classes, with effects persisting through at least 1960.

STT-0473.title: Product-liability chill on US innovation (1980s–1990s)
STT-0473.desc_html: In the 1980s and 1990s, high expected product liability costs depressed US innovation, terminating or reducing research (in domains such as contraceptive products), or reducing production of various technologies (e.g. the number of US firms producing vaccines for childhood diseases fell from 13 to 3 in the 1980s; a similar affect befell US private aircraft production)
